newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Valeo not unhappy with CGIP.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Valeo not unhappy with CGIP.

text.p: Valeo chairman Noel Goutard said he was not unhappy at the prospect of French holding company CGIP purchasing a 28 percent stake in the car parts company held by Italian businessman Carlo De Benedetti.
Goutard told Reuters he did not believe CGIP's interest represented just a political solution and said Valeo's long-term interest did not require a linkup with a bigger parts supplier.
"We have been loyal to our shareholders and we will always have the same loyalty to our shareholders," he said in an interview when asked about CGIP. He also hinted that he was likely to stay on.
"My mandate runs for three more years...I haven't sensed any hostile sign from them toward me," he said.
"I don't agree it's a 'political solution'. There have been political remarks. It's normal for the public authorities and for our clients to express their view," he said.

He also rejected the notion that Valeo needed an industrial partner to keep up with the components industry's rapid consolidation. "We have the necessary critical mass in almost all the areas we're in," he said. "Marrying an airbag producer wouldn't help us. It would bring no synergies in areas where we're leaders," such as engine cooling systems, he said.

Goutard said carmakers are now organised by function and merely increasing components activities is not the group's approach. "The strength of Valeo is that we treat each segment separately," he said.
The company has been the focus of controversy since De Benedetti put his stake up for sale nearly a year ago.

Foreign companies such as General Motors Corp and TRW Inc were reported at various times to be interested in a possible buyout of Valeo, but French carmakers threatened a boycott if Valeo were acquired by an outsider. The government also pushed for a "French solution".

Last week CGIP said its board sought to conclude a deal to buy the stake from De Benedetti's holding group Cerus. It did not disclose an offer price but said it expected to finance the purchase in part by selling half of its 20 percent stake in Crown Cork & Seal.
Goutard declined to comment whether other groups were in talks with Cerus on the stake.
PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet reiterated on Tuesday that it was important to preserve France's leading industrial companies.
Goutard said Valeo was on track to show a sales increase this year of 13 percent. "Maybe we're being a little pessimistic," he said.

He was less gloomy in his 1997 car industry outlook than others in the sector. "We're beginning the year under better economic conditions, already visible in Germany, and we have the lowest interest rates in a generation. These are not negative elements," he said.
